I have been farming my 5 mu here in Quzhou for 25 years, since I finished middle school and came back to work the land with my father. I grow winter wheat and then summer maize — that is the only system that makes sense on this soil. Last year my wheat gave me about 510 kg per mu and the maize did about 580 kg per mu. This year I will stick close to what worked, because changing things is risky and a bad harvest means real trouble for my family.

For wheat, I will rotary till the field after the maize stubble comes off in September, then sow improved seed in October. I buy improved varieties from the input dealer — I stopped saving my own seed years ago because the new stuff yields better, and all my neighbors use it too. For fertilizer, I will spread one full bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base, that is 50 kg per mu. The bags are usually 16-16-8 or close to it, whatever the dealer has in stock. Then when the wheat greens up in spring and hits the jointing stage, I will topdress with about 20 kg of urea per mu. I know that is a solid dose of nitrogen, but I would rather see the wheat grow dark green and strong than watch it go yellow and thin. I will irrigate three times: once for wintering if the soil is dry, once at jointing when the wheat drinks the most, and once at grain filling. For chemicals, I will spray herbicide once in early spring, and if the weather turns wet or I see insects, I will spray fungicide or insecticide once around heading.

For summer maize, I will plant hybrid seed immediately after wheat harvest in early June — there is no time to waste before the summer rains. I will not till again; I will no-till plant straight into the wheat stubble to save time and keep the moisture. I will put down about 30 kg of compound fertilizer per mu with the seeder. The make-or-break time is the big trumpet stage, when the ear is forming inside the stalk — that is when I will topdress with about 25 kg of urea per mu. I will irrigate twice: once at big trumpet and once at grain filling. Right after emergence I will spray herbicide, and I will watch for corn borer — if I see moths or my neighbor sprays, I will spray insecticide once.

My household has four people. My son and daughter-in-law work off-farm in Handan and send some money home, so I have cash for inputs, but I still count every yuan carefully. On 5 mu, every bag of fertilizer is a real expense. The well is my own, so water only costs me electricity. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than risk losing yield — fertilizer waste is just money, but an empty granary is a disaster. I expect my wheat to reach about 530 kg per mu and my maize to hit about 590 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.
